entry.name: standalone
entry.description: The standalone object lets you set options for creating a standalone application from a Max patch, and is used in conjunction with the Build Application/Collective... item found in the File menu. You should only have one standalone object in your top-level patch.

attributes.name: allwindowsactive
attributes.digest: Initial All Windows Active setting (Windows systems only)
attributes.description: Controls the initial setting of All Windows Active when the standalone is launched.

attributes.name: annotation
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: appicon_mac
attributes.digest: MacOS Application Icon (.icns)
attributes.description: Specify an .icns file as the standalone's application icon on MacOS.

attributes.name: appicon_win
attributes.digest: Windows Application Icon (.ico)
attributes.description: Specify an .ico file as the standalone's application icon on Windows.

attributes.name: background
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: bundleidentifier
attributes.digest: Bundle Identifier
attributes.description: The unique identifier string provided to the OS for your application bundle, e.g. "com.mycompany.myappname".

attributes.name: cantclosetoplevelpatchers
attributes.digest: Prevent closing top-level patcher
attributes.description: When selected, this option renders it impossible to close the top-level patcher in the standalone you build.

attributes.name: cefsupport
attributes.digest: CEF Support
attributes.description: Enables Max's CEF support for theobject in the standalone. Disable to reduce standalone size.

attributes.name: color
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: copysupport
attributes.digest: Include C74 Resources
attributes.description: When enabled, Max will copy additional resources to the standalone's support folder, including a full set of externals, shaders, Javascript support files, etc. Disable to reduce standalone size. Note that extensions and MIDI/audio externals are always included, even if this option is disabled.

attributes.name: database
attributes.digest: Database Support
attributes.description: Enables Max's file database support in the standalone.

attributes.name: fontface
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: fontname
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: fontsize
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: gensupport
attributes.digest: Gen Support
attributes.description: Enables Max's support for,,andobjects. Disable to reduce standalone size.

attributes.name: hidden
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: hint
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: ignoreclick
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: jspainterfile
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: noloadbangdefeating
attributes.digest: Allow loadbang override
attributes.description: When a patch is opened, the action of theobject can be disabled if you hold down the Command and Shift keys (Macintosh) or Control and Shift keys (Windows). When checked, this option will make your standalone always perform loadbang actions regardless of the state of the keyboard.

attributes.name: overdrive
attributes.digest: Initial overdrive setting
attributes.description: Controls the initial setting ofwhen the standalone is launched.

attributes.name: patching_rect
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: position
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: preffilename
attributes.digest: Preference file name
attributes.description: Save default settings for a standalone application to a custom Preference folder who's name is specified by a symbol. When the standalone is opened, it will save the standalone's preferences to a folder located at ~/Library/Application Support/[preffilename] (Mac) or C:\Users\[Your username]\AppData\Roaming\[preffilename] (Windows). If this is not set, standalone preferences will default to creating a folder within ~/Library/Application Support/Cycling '74 or C:\Users\[Your username]\AppData\Roaming\Cycling '74 named for the application.

attributes.name: presentation
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: presentation_rect
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: rect
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: searchformissingfiles
attributes.digest: Find files on search path
attributes.description: When checked, Max will use the search path to look for files that are not included in the collective inside your standalone. This includes objects that may not be present in a patch but are called on by Max to support the proper functioning of included objects. For example, the JSUI object requires various jitter objects to work, but does not require you to instantiate them in the patch.The primary reason to disable searching for missing files is to test your standalone to see if it includes all the necessary files to work if you move it to another machine.Please be aware that this option must be enabled (as it is by default) in order for users of your standalone application to be able to drag and drop files or otherwise use files not inluded in your application.

attributes.name: size
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: statusvisible
attributes.digest: Toggles displaying a Status window (similar to the Max Console)

attributes.name: textcolor
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: textjustification
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: usesearchpath
attributes.digest: Add search path subfolders
attributes.description: When checked, the standalone will create a search path consisting of all subfolders of the folder containing the application. Leaving this option unchecked is primarily of interest to Mac users, who might wish to put their standalone into the Applications folder, but avoid the startup cost of adding all the subfolders of the Applications folder to the search path. On Windows, the application is inside its own folder, so there usually are an insignificant number of subfolders to worry about.

attributes.name: varname
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).
